The following lists events that happened during '''2000 in South Africa'''.

==Incumbents==
* [[President of South Africa|President]]: [[Thabo Mbeki]].<ref name="FSA">[http://www.archontology.org/nations/south_africa/00_1994_td_s.php Archontology.org: A Guide for Study of Historical Offices: South Africa: Heads of State: 1994-2017] (Accessed on 5 June 2017)</ref>
* [[Deputy President of South Africa|Deputy President]]: [[Jacob Zuma]].
* [[Chief Justice of South Africa|Chief Justice]]: [[Ismail Mahomed]] then vacant.

=== [[Cabinet of South Africa|Cabinet]] ===
The Cabinet, together with the [[President of South Africa|President]] and the [[Deputy President of South Africa|Deputy President]], forms part of the Executive.{{Main article|First Cabinet of Thabo Mbeki}}

==Events==
;February
* Tropical [[Cyclone Eline]] brings heavy rains to [[Mozambique]], South Africa, [[Zimbabwe]], Botswana, [[Zambia]], Malawi and [[Madagascar]].
* The Mozambican navy begins evacuating people from low ground using rubber boats donated from last year's floods.
* 5 &ndash; The first wave of floods hit Mozambique.
* 9 &ndash; The [[South African Air Force]] airlifts foreign tourists cut off by floodwaters in the [[Kruger National Park]].
* 11 &ndash; [[Mbabane]], the capital of Swaziland, is left without drinking water due to flooding.
* 11 &ndash; The swollen [[Limpopo River]] bursts its banks.
* 11 &ndash; Southern Botswana receives 75% of its average annual rainfall in three days.
* 11 &ndash; United Nations officials say the lives of 150,000 people are in immediate danger from lack of food and disease.
* 22 &ndash; The full force of tropical Cyclone Eline hits the Mozambique coast near Beira, just north of the areas already devastated by the first wave of floods. Winds measure 260&nbsp;km/h (160&nbsp;mph).
* 22 &ndash; The South African air force sends in 5 helicopters to aid people trapped by floods.
* 24 &ndash; The United Nations says $13&nbsp;million is needed for urgent relief supplies.
* 24 &ndash; Mozambique calls for international help and asks for more than $65&nbsp;million to help rebuild the country's roads, bridges and power supplies.
* 27 &ndash; Zimbabwe opens the sluice gates of the [[Kariba Dam]].
* 27 &ndash; A wall of water about 2 metres (6&nbsp;ft) high hits [[Chokwe, Mozambique|Chokwe]] and inundate low farmlands around Chokwe and [[Xai-Xai]] in Mozambique.

;March
* 1 &ndash; The first [[United States Air Force]] [[C-17 Globemaster III|C-17]] transport aircraft lands in [[Maputo]].
* 1 &ndash; Britain states that it will send in food, medicine, equipment, 77 rubber boats and three [[Aérospatiale Puma|HC-1 Puma]] helicopters to help the South African helicopters.
* 1 &ndash; The South African Air Force sends 3 more helicopters to Mozambique.
* 2 &ndash; Cyclone Gloria hits the already flooded Mozambique.
* 2 &ndash; Aid workers in Mozambique estimate 100,000 people need to be evacuated and around 7,000 are trapped in trees. Many have been there for several days without food and water.
* 2 &ndash; Floodwater levels are said to have risen between 4 and 5 metres (more than 26 feet) in five days.
* 5 &ndash; Johannes Maremane wins his first national title in the men's marathon, clocking 2:11:15 in [[Pinelands, Cape Town|Pinelands]].
* 15 &ndash; The South African rescue workers end their operation in Mozambique.
* 16 – One of South Africa's worst serial killers, [[Cedric Maake]], is convicted of 27 murders as well as multiple armed robberies and rapes. Known as the Wemmer Pan serial killer, after the [[Johannesburg]] suburb where most of the murders took place, he is jailed at the [[High Court of South Africa|High Court]] for 1,340 years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Serial killer jailed for 1,340 years |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/africa/679141.stm |access-date=10 September 2023 |date=16 March 2000}}</ref>
* 28 &ndash; The [[Zambezi River]] is still between 2,5 metres and 3 metres above flood level.
* 28 &ndash; [[Cahora Bassa]] reduces water discharges.

;April
* 4 &ndash; South African soap opera [[7de Laan]] debuts on [[SABC 2]].
* 15 &ndash; The [[South African Air Force]] Museum's [[Supermarine Spitfire|Supermarine Spitfire MkIX]] no. 5553 is destroyed in an emergency landing during an airshow at [[AFB Swartkop]]. Pilot Lieutenant Colonel Neil Thomas survives with minor injuries.
* [[Nicky Boje]], [[Hansie Cronje]], [[Herschelle Gibbs]], [[Pieter Strydom]] and [[Henry Williams (cricketer)|Henry Williams]], along with a number of other international [[cricket]] players and Indian [[bookmaker]]s, are accused by the New Delhi police of cheating, fraud and [[criminal conspiracy]] in alleged [[match fixing]].

;May
* 19 &ndash; President [[Thabo Mbeki]] is awarded an honorary doctorate of laws from the [[Glasgow Caledonian University]].

;July
* 9–14 &ndash; The 13th International AIDS conference is held in [[Durban]], [[KwaZulu-Natal]], the first ever to be held in a developing country.

;August
* 21 &ndash; A [[South African Air Force]] [[Aermacchi MB-326|MB-326K Impala Mk II]] crashes during a routine night training flight. Pilot Lt. Dian Smit is killed.
* 22 &ndash; President Thabo Mbeki is voted Newsmaker of the Year by the Pretoria Press Club.

;September
* 27 &ndash; South Africa and India sign a [[memorandum of understanding]] on defence co-operation.

;November
* 10 &ndash; A memorandum of understanding is signed for the creation of the [[Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park|Gaza-Kruger-Gonarezhou Transfrontier Park]].
* 27 &ndash; A [[South African Air Force]] [[Atlas Cheetah|Atlas Cheetah C]] crashes on finals to [[AFB Makhado]] killing Capt. Piet Koster.
* [[Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh]] and [[Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh|Prince Edward, Earl of Wessex]] visit South Africa.

;Unknown date
* The [[Democratic Party (South Africa)|Democratic Party]] joins with the [[New National Party (South Africa)|New National Party]] to form the [[Democratic Alliance (South Africa)|Democratic Alliance]].
* The [[Gordon Institute of Business Science]] is established by the [[University of Pretoria]].<ref>[http://www.gibs.co.za/about-us/who-are-we.aspx Gordon Institute of Business Science] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110824121908/http://www.gibs.co.za/about-us/who-are-we.aspx |date=24 August 2011 }} Retrieved 25 June 2011</ref>
